summary_md:
**2/2, 90%, 😌.** About 5 minutes in total: **8 plays** at normal speed (1×), you opened the words after **2 min 15 s**, and you replayed only **one line, twice** – line 7: *"I also met my neighbours. Margaret lives downstairs and knows everyone on the street."* Why that line: it is **two sentences in one breath**, *met my* joins into one sound (/metmaɪ/ – the **t** is almost silent), and *knows everyone* links into /noʊzˈevriwʌn/. Everything else you caught.

But be careful with the number: you **read this same message 20 minutes earlier**, so 90% here measures your *memory* as much as your *ears*. It does **not** count as a first-listen score – your real first-listen level is still **B1** (dialogue ~90%, narration ~70%).
asks_md:
**"Listen giống hệt reading thì dễ đoán quá – nên soạn bài khác, tương tự hoặc phần kế tiếp nhưng ở dạng listen."** You're right, and the research agrees with you: when you already know the text, your brain **predicts** instead of **listening**, so the ear does less work. Reading first only helps when the listening is *new* but on a *known topic* (same people, same words, new information) – that's called **narrow listening**. 🇻🇳 Đọc rồi nghe lại y nguyên = tai được 'nhắc bài', không phải tự bắt âm.

**What I changed tonight:**
- **2026-11-13-11** (still to do) was the *same article as audio* → I rewrote it: now it's a **new conversation** – Nam and Claire's Friday chat, Claire gives 3 tips for week 2. Same topic, all new information.
- **From now on:** a 🎧 lesson after a 📖 lesson = the **next part** or **another side** of the story (a conversation, a phone call, another person's view) – never the same text. The same text only appears again in *Play today* (on the go), if you want it.
- I also added a rule to my checklist tool so this can't happen again.
